newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht near record low onshore late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht near record low onshore late.

text.p: The Thai baht was near a record low level onshore late on Wednesday as commercial demand for dollars continued to pressure the currency despite afternoon intervention by the Bank of Thailand, traders said.
The baht was at 32.25/32.55 per dollar at 1100 GMT despite central bank intervention during the afternoon at around the 32.60 level, dealers said.
Commercial demand for dollars saw the recently floated currency adopt a weaker tone after opening at a previous record low on Wednesday morning at 31.60 per dollar, dealers said.
The interbank overnight offered rate was steady in the 15-18 percent range after the passing of a reserve period on Tuesday.
Dealers said the interbank rate softened to the current rate partly because it was guided by the central bank's bond repurchase market.
Some commercial banks preferred to invest in the repo market and became very cautious in lending in the market due to ongoing financial woes.
